questions.stem: Given set A = {1, 2, 3} and set B = {3, 4, 5}, what is the union of sets A and B (A ∪ B)?
questions.solution: The union of sets A and B (A ∪ B) includes all elements that are in either set A or set B. So the union is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.
questions.explanation: Union operation combines all unique elements from both sets without repetition.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing 'A' or 'B', which are subsets of the correct answer and do not include all elements. The union should contain all unique elements from both sets.

questions.stem: Set X = {a, b, c} and set Y = {c, d, e}. What is the result of X ∪ Y?
questions.solution: The union of sets X and Y (X ∪ Y) is {a, b, c, d, e}. The element 'c' appears in both sets but is only included once in the union.
questions.explanation: Union operation combines all unique elements from both sets without repetition.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing 'B', which omits elements 'a' and 'b' that are part of set X. The union should contain all unique elements from both sets.
